          Liverpool vs Brighton Prediction: Premier League Preview
        
      
                          
                      Oct 23, 2026
          
                      Tom Webber / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
We look ahead to this Premier League match at Anfield with our Liverpool vs Brighton prediction and preview. Can the Seagulls continue their impressive form?
Liverpool will hope their new-found momentum will help them stop Brighton & Hove Albion in their tracks when they meet in the Premier League on Sunday.

Andoni Iraola's side bounced back from a 3-0 loss at home to Manchester City after the international break by coming from behind to beat Brentford 2-1 last weekend. The goals from Víctor Muñoz and Alexander Isak arrived after the Bees were reduced to 10 men at the Gtech Community Stadium.

The Reds backed that up by beating Villarreal in the Champions League on Tuesday. That time they had to recover from two goals down, but still managed to seal a 4-3 victory that kept their 100% record in Europe this season intact.

Villarreal boss Iñigo Pérez acknowledged that the Anfield atmosphere played a role in his team's capitulation, even though it has not been quite as much of a fortress for Liverpool in the Premier League.

They are winless in their last five Premier League home matches (D4 L1), their only worse runs at Anfield being a seven-game stretch from November 2002 to February 2003 and an eight-game streak between December 2020 and March 2021.

Florian Wirtz has been a target for criticism for a perceived lack of threat, but the Germany international has created the most chances both overall (20) and from open play (18) in the Premier League this season, while he came off the bench to score his first goal of the season on Tuesday.

Isak finally appears to be hitting his stride at Anfield too, having scored five goals in as many Premier League appearances. The Swede lost four of his first five games for Liverpool but they are unbeaten in his past 15 appearances (W9 D6).

Yet Brighton's recent form means that Liverpool ending their wait for a home victory in the top flight is in no way a given. Fabian Hürzeler's side have been in stunning form, leading the Premier League scoring charts and winning their past four top-flight fixtures by an aggregate score of 15-0.

That includes a 3-0 win against reigning champions Arsenal and 5-0 victories over Coventry City and rivals Crystal Palace, in which Diego Gómez scored an incredible goal from the halfway line. With two victories by at least five goals in their past four matches, Brighton have equalled the amount they managed across their prior 376 league games combined.
A much-changed line-up was held to an uneventful 0-0 draw by Jablonec in the UEFA Conference League on Thursday, ending their six-game winning run in all competitions.

But Hürzeler used the game – his 100th in charge of the club – to rest some key players. One of those was Charalampos Kostoulas, who has scored and assisted in two of his last three Premier League appearances.

Kostoulas is the first teenager to score and assist in the same game more than once in a season since Kelechi Iheanacho for City in 2016-17, and could become the first since Michael Owen in 1998-99 to do it three times.

The Greek will likely play from the start after being an unused substitute against Jablonec, but Evan Ferguson, Stefanos Tzimas, Kaoru Mitoma, Zadok Yohanna and Yankuba Minteh – reportedly a summer target for Liverpool – remain sidelined.
Mats Wieffer could recover from his knee injury in time to feature, while Femi Azeez and Pascal Struijk will also hope to play a part after missing out on Thursday.

Liverpool have slight concerns over Bradley Barcola and Muñoz, while Jeremie Frimpong and Dominik Szoboszlai remained sidelined along with long-term absentees Conor Bradley, Giovanni Leoni and Hugo Ekitiké.

Brighton are in a rich vein of form and have performed well against Liverpool recently, winning two of their last three Premier League meetings with the Reds – as many as they won in their first 15 encounters with them.

While the Seagulls were 2-1 winners in their most clash at the Amex Stadium in March, Liverpool beat them twice at Anfield last season – triumphing 2-0 in the Premier League in December and 3-0 in the fourth round of the FA Cup two months later.
In total, Liverpool have lost just one of their last 13 home games against Brighton in all competitions, winning each of the last four at Anfield.
Liverpool's strong recent home form against the Seagulls is likely a contributing factor in the Opta supercomputer's calculation that they have a 46.8% win probability.
